rationale: bugs_open/134: the documentation convention for 'optional' (a trailing '?') leaked from a seed comment into two real JSON config key names, so product-spec-refresher's refresh_specs step carries "category?" and "limit?" while the action reads category and limit — neither key has ever resolved. Re-verified live 2026-08-03: the row still carries both keys, the agent has 0 runs in all retained history, the fleet punctuation sweep still returns exactly these 2 rows, and no Go code anywhere reads a '?'-suffixed key. The fix is three-part, ordered by what closes the door: (1) correct the data at both sources — seed 156 (a replay must restore correctness, not the defect) and the live row via migration 298 modelled on 296's snapshot/guard/DO-RAISE-verify shape; (2) opt the action into the existing SCR-003 contract with CheckConfig: true — its spec already enumerates every key its step carries, so opting in asserts nothing new and the next typo becomes a warning instead of six silent months; (3) close the CLASS with a --suspicious-keys mode on cmd/config-key-audit: a top-level step-config key containing '?', '*', a space or ':' is doc-notation punctuation and never readable, for every action INCLUDING the ~151 not opted into SCR-003 — which is exactly the population where this instance sat invisible since 07-15. Behaviour-change call, stated: correcting the keys makes caller-supplied category/limit start resolving. Nothing depends on current behaviour (0 runs ever, no scheduled_tasks row) and the seed's own header documents {site_id, category?} as the intended contract, so the change realises the author's stated intent. When no caller passes them, behaviour is byte-identical (action defaults gripper/20). Deliberately NOT done: declaring 'category?'/'limit?' in the spec (the WRONG_CALLS 2026-07-28 trap — declaring a dead key silences the detector); touching the runtime validator fleet-wide (an offline advisory report needs no shared-guarantee change). No ordering constraint: the deployed image has registered refresh_product_specs since 07-15, so the data fix works against the current binary; Go changes ride the next roll.

plan.summary: Two live config keys carry a doc-notation '?' suffix and therefore never resolve; fix the seed and the live row so the keys match what the action reads, opt the action into unknown-config-key detection, and add an offline audit mode that flags doc-notation punctuation in any live step-config key fleet-wide, including actions that have not opted into the declared-contract check.

edits.rationale: Opt the action into unknown-config-key detection. Its spec already enumerates every key the step config carries (site_id, category, limit), and ExtractActionInputs reads config[k] for every Required/Optional key, so per action_inputs.go's own guidance CheckConfig asserts nothing new — it only arms the existing validator and the offline report for this action.
The seed is what a rebuild reads; a replay of 156 unfixed restores the defect. Line 15's comment ('{site_id, category?}') is documentation notation and stays; only the two JSON keys change.

The live agent_definitions row has the same two dead keys. Migration modelled on 296's shape: snapshot_agent first, guarded idempotent UPDATE (fenced on the bad keys being present), doc_notes record, DO/RAISE verify blocks asserting both the fixed keys AND neighbours (site_id mapping unchanged, sibling steps intact — a verify that only checks its own key cannot tell a surgical edit from a flattening write), live BEGIN/COMMIT, rollback comment.
edits.sketch:
BEGIN;
SELECT snapshot_agent('product-spec-refresher', '298: pre-update');
UPDATE agent_definitions
SET default_config = jsonb_set(
      default_config #- '{workflow,steps,refresh_specs,config,category?}'
                     #- '{workflow,steps,refresh_specs,config,limit?}',
      '{workflow,steps,refresh_specs,config}',
      ((default_config #> '{workflow,steps,refresh_specs,config}')
        - 'category?' - 'limit?')
        || jsonb_build_object('category', 'input_data.category',
                              'limit', 'input_data.limit'),
      false)
WHERE type = 'product-spec-refresher'
  AND is_active AND COALESCE(is_snapshot,false)=false AND deleted_at IS NULL
  AND default_config #> '{workflow,steps,refresh_specs,config}' ? 'category?';
-- doc_notes INSERT (migration category), then:
DO $$ ... RAISE EXCEPTION unless config has category+limit, lacks 'category?'/'limit?',
   site_id mapping = 'site_record.site_id', and steps ensure_site_record/complete survive $$;
COMMIT;

edits.rationale: Close the class, not the instance. CheckConfig only protects opted-in actions; this defect lived on an action outside that population for six weeks. A top-level step-config key containing '?', '*', a space or ':' is schema-doc punctuation and is never a readable key for ANY action (grep: no Go reads such a key), so it is reportable without the action's opt-in. Same house pattern as --unregistered-actions: a flag on this binary (the council's own two-seats precedent against second binaries), pure function separated from I/O, same stdin export, walked with validation.WalkSteps so nested sub-workflow steps are covered, refuse an empty decode, exit 1 on findings. Character set kept to exactly the four the bug's sweep used, so the check starts green post-migration and a future hit is signal.

Fixture test in the findUnregisteredActions style: a fixture carrying 'category?' at top level and a '?' key inside a loop sub-workflow must both be flagged (the nested case is bugs_open/144's blindness — assert it explicitly); clean keys including dotted and underscored ones must not be. The test fails if the check is removed, which is the mutation-proof.

The report is where sessions already look; a fourth section makes the class check run whenever the coverage report runs, against the WORKFLOWS_JSON the script already fetched. Script exits 1 if either unknown keys or suspicious keys are found (both are real inert-key defects, unlike the undeclared-actions coverage gap).
edits.sketch:
SUSPICIOUS="$(printf '%s' "$WORKFLOWS_JSON" | (cd "$REPO_ROOT" && go run ./cmd/config-key-audit --suspicious-keys))"
rc_susp=$?
# printed as '=== SUSPICIOUS KEYS (doc-notation punctuation — never readable) ==='
# section body: the JSON findings, or 'none'; final exit ORs this with the unknown-keys result

grounded_in: bugs_open/134: 'So neither key ever resolves. limit silently takes its hard-coded default of 20 and category is empty, whatever the caller passes in input_data. No Go code anywhere reads a ?-suffixed key.'

Live DB 2026-08-03: refresh_specs config = {"limit?": "input_data.limit", "site_id": "site_record.site_id", "category?": "input_data.category"}; orchestration_states runs for product-spec-refresher = 0; punctuation sweep = 2 rows, both this step.

refresh_product_specs_action.go:211-215: category := inputs.Get("category") ... limit := inputs.GetInt("limit", 20); spec at :175-178 has Required [site_id], Optional [category, limit, delay_ms, llm_model], no CheckConfig.

That extractor reads config[k] for every Required and Optional key ... so for such an action the spec is already a verified statement of what it reads from config and opting in asserts nothing new.'

seed 156 line 15 (comment): '-- {site_id, category?}. Requires the chassis image that registers' — the doc notation the key names were copied from; lines 60-61 carry "category?"/"limit?" inside the real JSON.

cmd/config-key-audit/main.go header: 'It is a FLAG rather than a second binary because the council gate's editquality and reuse_agent seats both objected to the second binary independently (2026-07-28, corr 07cf67c6)'.
WRONG_CALLS.md 2026-07-28 (via bugs_open/134 candidate 3): declaring a dead key makes it recognised and silences the detector, leaving the behaviour broken and the report clean.
plan.risks: 1) The migration touches agent_definitions.default_config with jsonb surgery — the verify blocks assert neighbours at two levels (the site_id mapping and sibling steps) precisely so a flattening write cannot pass; snapshot_agent runs first so rollback is a restore. 2) Behaviour change: a future caller passing category/limit will now be honoured — intended per the seed's own contract; with 0 runs ever and no schedule, nothing observed can regress. 3) The suspicious-key character set is deliberately only ?/*/space/colon — a doc convention using other punctuation would pass; reviewers should judge whether that narrowness is right (it matches the only convention observed in this estate, and a wider net risks flagging a legitimate future key shape). 4) scripts/audit-config-keys.sh gains an exit-1 path; its consumers are humans and sessions, not CI gates (checked: grep finds no automated caller), so a new failure mode does not break a pipeline. 5) CheckConfig makes the runtime validator warn on unknown keys for this action after the next roll — warning only, StrictConfig deliberately not set.
